ev.q: CDC analyzed national surveillance data for 2002
the rate of P&S syphilis increased 9.1% (from 2.2 cases per 100,000 population in 2001 to 2.4 cases in 2002)
2,534 (80.7%) reported no cases of P&S syphilis
the South had the highest rate of P&S syphilis (3.1 cases per 100,000 population) in 2002
The male-to-female rate ratio increased in 27 states and the District of Columbia.
the male-to-female rate ratio increased among non-Hispanic whites (from 6.0 to 11.0)
CDC analyzed surveillance data for syphilis cases reported weekly to health departments nationwide in 2002
During 2001--2002, the rate of P&S syphilis decreased 10.9% among non-Hispanic blacks

methods_quotes.q: P&S syphilis rates were calculated by using population denominators from the U.S. Bureau of the Census
Data on reported cases of P&S syphilis were analyzed because these cases represented incidence
